images.title: 37 moves left on the place value board
images.purpose: Show that multiplying 37 by 10 and by 100 moves every digit one and two places to the left and puts zeros in the empty places.
images.composition: A place value table of three rows: 37, then 370 and then 3,700, with the row sentences at the left and the digit tiles moving left row by row.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. One place value table with 4 columns and a header row. The header row spans x 560 to 1320 and y 120 to 210, with 4 header cells each 190 px wide filled grey #6B7280 and the white bold sans-serif (30 px) names Thousands, Hundreds, Tens and Ones centred in them, from left to right, at x 655, 845, 1035 and 1225. Under the header there are exactly 3 rows, each 120 px tall, spanning x 560 to 1320: row 1 y 210 to 330, row 2 y 330 to 450, row 3 y 450 to 570. Every cell has a 2 px dark #2B2B2B outline and no fill. Digit tiles are rounded squares (corner radius 14 px) 84 by 84 px, centred in their cells, with a bold sans-serif digit (56 px). The digits 3 and 7 are on teal #0072B2 tiles with white digits; the zeros are on amber #E69F00 tiles with dark #1F2937 digits. Row 1 (centre y 270): a 3 in the Tens cell and a 7 in the Ones cell, the Thousands and Hundreds cells empty. Row 2 (centre y 390): a 3 in the Hundreds cell, a 7 in the Tens cell and an amber 0 in the Ones cell, the Thousands cell empty. Row 3 (centre y 510): a 3 in the Thousands cell, a 7 in the Hundreds cell, an amber 0 in the Tens cell and an amber 0 in the Ones cell. In all there are 9 tiles: 6 teal (3 and 7 three times) and 3 amber zeros. To the left of the table, left aligned at x 80, the row labels in dark bold sans-serif: row 1 the number 37 at y 270 (48 px); row 2 the sentence 37 × 10 = 370 at y 380 (44 px) with the words 1 place to the left under it at y 425 (30 px, regular); row 3 the sentence 37 × 100 = 3,700 at y 500 (44 px) with the words 2 places to the left under it at y 545 (30 px, regular). No other text anywhere. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a row with digits in other cells than the cells named, or a zero tile that is not amber
images.takeaway: Multiplying by 10 moves every digit one place to the left and multiplying by 100 moves it two places, and zeros fill the empty places.
images.description: A place value table with 37, then 370 and then 3,700, each digit tile one more place to the left.
images.context: Concept image for Multiplying by 10 and 100. It follows the idea of the place value tables in your maths book and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 37.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student follow the 3 and the 7 from row to row and count the places they moved. The slip to watch: saying that a zero is simply added at the end, without seeing that every digit moved.

image_decisions.why: The three rows of the board make the move of every digit visible, which the words add a zero hide.
